$comment: False positives and deliberate non-translatables for scripts/i18n-inventory.mjs. Every entry needs a reason; tests/i18n-inventory.node.test.ts rejects a missing reason and an entry that matches nothing. Match is substring on the finding text, exact on file and (when present) category.

exceptions.reason: Allen-Bradley controller family name — an industrial product identifier. PS-I18N-001 §2 and ADR-0001 §6 keep industrial units, signal names and stable IDs untranslated.
Allen-Bradley controller family name — industrial product identifier, not UI copy.

SEW gearmotor type designation from the bundled AASX digital nameplate — a device model number that must match the asset, so translating it would break the link to the datasheet.
Product name in the version footer. Translating a brand would make the build string unsearchable in support threads and release notes; the surrounding tooltip IS translated (settings:version.title).

Deliberately bilingual, for the same reason the locale list uses endonyms (LanguageSection.tsx): whoever needs this control cannot read the language the UI is currently in. Routing it through the catalog would render it in one language only — and would put CJK in en-US, which tests/i18n-catalog.node.test.ts rejects.
Sample signal path shown as a preview of each chip variant. PS-I18N-001 §2 / ADR-0001 §6 keep signal names untranslated, so a translated example would show a form no PLC ever emits.

Placeholder mirroring MULTIUSER_DEFAULTS.displayName ('Browser' in multiuser-settings-store.ts). It has to match the value that is actually sent to peers, so translating it would advertise a name the session never uses.
